_comment: marble_spikes_strip, STRIP: the same spike patch on a 6.0 x 2.0 m slab 0.10 m thick -- a spiked threshold laid across a lane. Seven cells by two, a spike stitched into every one: the pit's own pedestal-ring-and-pyramid cell (marble_lane_build), the pit's taper (marble_build.BASE_K) and its small spike at every third foot, cones 1.2..2.2 m tall on a 0.12 m plinth; the tallest tip is at y 2.42. Built by marble_spikes_build.py under --variant strip; marble_spikes_strip_build.py is the shim that names it. ORIGIN IS THE BASE CENTRE, length along local X, y=0 the floor it sits on. ONE material: marble_build's painted 256 px atlas, zones field/spike/plinth/shade. HAZARD, NOT COVER -- MarbleSpikesCollision (the node name is the same in both footprints) is the SLAB ONLY, a closed 6.0 x 2.0 x 0.10 m box shipped as a `-colonly` node; the spikes are not colliders, exactly as they are not in the pit. THE LETHAL VOLUME IS THE SCENE'S: put an Area3D over this model with a BoxShape3D of size (6.0, 2.6, 2.0) centred 1.30 m above the model's origin (its roof clears the tallest tip, its floor is the slab), collision_layer 0 and collision_mask 1048577 -- living bodies and ghosts, as maps/marble/marble.tscn masks SpikeFloor -- handing whatever enters to MatchController.handle_fall(), the way scripts/match/kill_volume.gd does. NOT KillVolume itself: that node writes its own CYLINDER hanging below its origin, which is the fall case and the wrong shape for a strip. Godot turns the collider into a StaticBody3D + ConcavePolygonShape3D and drops its mesh, so `surfaces` counts only what is drawn.
